**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/eu-frames-one-day-open-science.html#/part-1-credibility-and-tools){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 1 asks what a claim in social science is for, why people describe the field as being in crisis, and what open research proposes to do about it. It brings in the evidence of the SCORE programme, the five Multi100 analysts of the claim that the day works on, and the archives, repositories and registries in which the data, code and plans of a study are kept. The browser lab is set up at the end, and runs into the first break, so that a machine that gives trouble costs no talk.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, the opening | The plan of the day, the two kinds of aim, and what you do not need: no installation, no git and no accounts. Open the browser lab in a tab and leave it to load. | 6 minutes |
| Slides, credibility | What social science is for; false positives and forking paths; the evidence from replications and many-analysts studies; incentives and questionable research practices, and why the worry is structural rather than a matter of fraud; the twenty-nine teams of the red-card study and their estimates; why 'replication' names three different operations. | 18 minutes |
| Slides, the vocabulary and open research | The matrix of data and analysis that separates reproduction, robustness and replication; repeatability and credibility; a quick check on the matrix in peer review; and the practices of open research, each with the obstacle that it removes. | 12 minutes |
| Slides, SCORE | The programme and its three studies, of reproducibility, robustness and replicability, each with its results, and why the three verdicts do not go together. | 18 minutes |
| Slides, Multi100 from the inside | What an analyst received, the paper in brief, the two Multi100 tasks and how their results are put on one scale, and a forest plot of the five analysts of the claim. | 14 minutes |
| Slides, open research infrastructures, and the [SCORE dossier](https://osf.io/h7432) on the OSF | Archives, statistical offices, repositories and registries; the data of the case and the terms on which they are held, which decide what a reproduction can use; then three minutes in the dossier, finding the deposit of the analyst whose result you will reproduce. | 12 minutes |
| Slides on the browser lab, then [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd) Task 1 | Run the setup cell until the panel of 270 country-years is in front of you; the warm-up on the three Rs fills the wait while R loads. | 10 minutes, and the 30-minute break after it if you need more |

**By the end of the part** the browser lab runs on your machine, you can tell apart the three operations that go under the single word 'replication', and you know where the materials of a published study are kept and on what terms.
